feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback shifts priority toward carbonyl response transfer. The m78 50/1 experiment had large historical underprediction of both endpoints, motivating a fixed-loading curve and a loading contrast. m28 again showed completion underprediction. The m125 results strengthen a ratio-dependent injection-volume interpretation: matched loading at 2/1 produced substantially different endpoints between 300 and 500 uL DCM. This does not establish a universal injection effect. Recent amino-nitrile labels were comparatively well predicted, reducing the marginal value of more nearby measurements this round. Conversely, m90 at 5/1 and m104 at 20/1 were overpredicted, weakening a blanket expectation of underestimated nitrogen-containing tails. The earlier structural description of m37 also needs correction: it is para-nitroacetophenone, not an amino ketone. These interpretations concern historical acquisition errors and measured outcomes, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines failure follow-up with experiments that test transfer across recurring catalog families. The m78 curve investigates the latest major failure and whether its weak-eluent behavior persists across loading. The m125 pair directly isolates injection volume. Nitrogen selections examine distinct unresolved response shapes, including a predicted plateau. New m27, m94, m201, m38, m194, and m21 pairs test structural transfer across aliphatic ketones, beta-ketoesters, nitro aromatics, fused aromatic ketones, and ether-containing compounds. The m59, m198, m99, and m131 pairs add solvent-response constraints around established chemical families, while m62 covers a distinct boronic ester environment. Matching conditions within pairs makes the labels more informative about response slopes than isolated novelty measurements. Both steep and modest predicted responses are included to improve interpolation and generalization across rows. Missing experimental variables and occasional inconsistent observations limit mechanistic attribution; these labels are intended to improve prediction under the recorded conditions, not optimize chromatographic performance.
